generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The test verifies the handler doesn't crash and that a reasonable volume of bytes is written, but it never inspects the actual sequence numbers in the emitted pcap packets. A more targeted assertion (e.g., capturing the `OutputStream` bytes and decoding the TCP header to confirm the sequence number wrapped past `0xFFFFFFFF` back into the low range) would guard against the off-by-one modulo issue and the copy-paste bug above. As written, the test would pass even if the wrap logic were subtly wrong.

Copy-paste bug: the second assignment writes to `sendSegmentNumber` instead of `receiveSegmentNumber`. As written, `sendSegmentNumber` is incremented twice (once with its own value, once with `receiveSegmentNumber`'s value) and `receiveSegmentNumber` is never updated.
```java
sendSegmentNumber = incrementUintSegmentNumber(sendSegmentNumber, 1);
sendSegmentNumber = incrementUintSegmentNumber(receiveSegmentNumber, 1); // should be receiveSegmentNumber = ...
```
Also, there are stray spaces before the commas in `sendSegmentNumber , receiveSegmentNumber ,` — minor, but worth cleaning up.

The modulo constant is off by one. TCP sequence numbers are 32-bit unsigned and wrap at 2^32 (i.e., the valid range is `[0, 0xFFFFFFFF]`, which contains 2^32 = `0x100000000` values). Using `% 0xFFFFFFFFL` means the value `0xFFFFFFFF` is never produced (it maps to 0), and the wrap point is shifted by one. For example, `0xFFFFFFFE + 2` should wrap to `0`, but with this formula it yields `1`.
Fix: use `(sequenceNumber + value) & 0xFFFFFFFFL` or `(sequenceNumber + value) % 0x100000000L`.

@normanmaurer I'll have time today to look into this and address any issues I find.

Found 2 issues directly related to this PR while using Wireshark to look at the generated 5GB pcap. Those will be addressed.

Noticed two other issues present in 4.1.

1. If the payload is larger than 65495 for TCP, the length field in the IP packet is incorrect due to the length being a ushort. UDP will have a similar problem.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155cec08-767f-4efc-a2c5-c9c04718bd75)
2. When the PcapWriteHandler is attached to a TCP server, the FIN messages have incorrect segment and ack numbers. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c3109-558d-4fa2-8cce-5fa05503ebc0)


I will try to find the time to address these here with unit tests

For TCP, the payload can just be split into multiple PCAP entries. 
For UDP, I imagine it could just log that it received too large of a payload.
Alright, all of the above have been handled. Tested large PCAP files and those show correctly in Wireshark now.
